Question Choices: State the intermediate value theorem in words.
Question Answers: a continuous function takes every value between its endpoint values|all intermediate values occur for a continuous function
Hints: Continuity prevents jumping over output values.|Use a closed interval and a target between endpoint outputs.
Solution: If f is continuous on [a,b] with a<b, it attains every output between f(a) and f(b). A target strictly between the endpoint values is attained at an interior input. Opposite signs bracket at least one zero; equal endpoint values are already attained at the endpoints. The conclusion is existence, not an exact formula for the input. A continuous function on [a, b] attains every value between f(a) and f(b).
